texts.3.2: On a certain day a pearl did I take up, my brethren;
texts.3.3: I saw in it mysteries pertaining to the Kingdom;
texts.3.4: Semblances and types of the Majesty;
texts.3.5: It became a fountain, and I drank out of it mysteries of the Son.
texts.3.6: I put it, my brethren, upon the palm of my hand,
texts.3.8: I went to look at it on one side,
texts.3.9: And it proved faces on all sides.
texts.3.10: I found out that the Son was incomprehensible,
texts.3.12: In its brightness I beheld the Bright One Who cannot be clouded,
texts.3.13: And in its pureness a great mystery,
texts.3.14: Even the Body of Our Lord which is well-refined:
texts.3.15: In its undivideness I saw the Truth
texts.3.17: It was so that I saw there its pure conception,
texts.3.18: The Church, and the Son within her.
texts.3.19: The cloud was the likeness of her that bare Him,
texts.3.21: Since there shone forth from her His gracious Shining.
texts.3.22: I saw therein his Trophies, and His victories, and His crowns.
texts.3.23: I saw His helpful and overflowing graces,
texts.3.24: And His hidden things with His revealed things.
texts.3.26: It was greater to me than the ark,
texts.3.28: I saw therein folds without shadow to them
texts.3.29: Because it was a daughter of light,
texts.3.32: A silent harp that without voice gave out melodies.
texts.3.33: The trumpet falters and the thunder mutters;
texts.3.35: Leave things hidden, take things revealed.
texts.3.36: Thou hast seen in the clear sky a second shower;
texts.3.40: And as that manna which alone filled the people,
texts.3.41: In the place of pleasant meats,
texts.3.43: So does this pearl fill me in the place of books,
texts.3.46: And when I asked if there were yet other mysteries,
texts.3.47: It had no mouth for me that I might hear from,
texts.3.48: Neither any ears wherewith it might hear me.
texts.3.49: O Thou thing without senses, whence I have gained new senses!
texts.3.52: "The daughter of the sea am I, the illimitable sea!
texts.3.53: And from that sea whence I came up it is
texts.3.54: That there is a mighty treasury of mysteries in my bosom!
texts.3.55: Search thou out the sea, but search not out the Lord of the sea!
texts.3.56: "I have seen the divers who came down after me, when astonied,
texts.3.57: So that from the midst of the sea they returned to the dry ground;
texts.3.58: For a few moments they sustained it not.
texts.3.59: Who would linger and be searching on into the depths of the Godhead?
texts.3.60: "The waves of the Son are full of blessing,
texts.3.62: Have ye not seen, then, the waves of the sea,
texts.3.63: Which if a ship should struggle with them would break her to pieces,
texts.3.64: And if she yield herself to them, and rebel not against them,
texts.3.66: In the sea all the Egyptians were choked, though they scrutinised it not,
texts.3.67: And, without prying, the Hebrews too were overcome upon the dry land,
texts.3.68: And how shall ye be kept alive?
texts.3.69: And the men of Sodom were licked up by the fire,
texts.3.71: "At these uproars the fish in the sea were moved,
texts.3.73: Have ye then a heart of stone
texts.3.74: That ye read these things and run into these errors?
texts.3.75: O great fear that justice also should be so long silent!"
texts.3.78: And whether of the two will prevail?
texts.3.81: Along with the fume of disputation
texts.3.82: And unto which shall we hearken?
texts.3.83: Prayer and prying from one mouth,
texts.3.84: And which shall we listen to?
texts.3.85: "For three days was Jonah a neighbour in the sea:
texts.3.86: The living things that were in the sea were affrighted,
texts.3.89: And ye are obstinate at your scrutiny of Him!'"
texts.4.3: Let thy stillness speak to one that hears;
texts.4.4: With silent mouth speak with us:
texts.4.5: For whoso hears the stammerings of thy silence,
texts.4.6: to him thy type utters its silent cry concerning our Redeemer.
texts.4.7: Thy mother is a virgin of the sea, though he took her not:
texts.4.8: She fell into his bosom, though he knew her not;
texts.4.9: She conceived thee near him, though he did not know her.
texts.4.10: Do thou, that art a type, reporach the Jewish women
texts.4.11: That have thee hung upon them.
texts.4.12: Thou art the only progeny of all forms
texts.4.13: Which art like to the Word on High,
texts.4.14: Whom singly the Most High begot.
texts.4.15: The engraven forms seem to be the type of created things above.
texts.4.16: This visible offspring of the invisible womb
texts.4.17: Is a type of great things.
